package.title: Tirzepatide Hair Loss: Will It Grow Back? #shorts
package.description:
Shedding linked to fast weight loss is often telogen effluvium: lots of hairs enter their resting phase at once. It usually starts 2–4 months after the trigger, and for most people hair regains its normal fullness within 6–9 months. Get checked if it lasts more than about 6 months, comes out in patches or your scalp looks scarred.

Don't stop or change your medicines on your own. Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
American Academy of Dermatology, Do you have hair loss or hair shedding? https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/hair-loss/insider/shedding
DermNet, Telogen effluvium: https://dermnetnz.org/topics/telogen-effluvium
NHS, Hair loss: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/hair-loss/

factcheck.summary: The script is accurate and safe. I checked all five sources and the claims match. DermNet says shedding is noticed 2 to 4 months after the trigger and tapers back to normal over 6–9 months in most cases. It lists weight loss and unusual diet as triggers and recommends correcting abnormal thyroid, iron, B12 and folate levels. It also recommends "plenty of protein" and says recovery "may be incomplete in some cases", which fits the hedge "usually isn't permanent". AAD says "within six to nine months, the hair tends to regain its normal fullness". The Zepbound label (revised 8/2026) links hair loss to weight reduction. Hair loss was 5% vs 1% on placebo, and no tirzepatide patients stopped treatment because of it. That supports calling the shedding "linked to fast weight loss" without saying the drug causes it. The script is hedged well ("often", "usually", "for most people"). It has the kidney caveat for protein and doesn't suggest supplements or dosing. It includes the don't-stop/change line, "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line, and it ends on the correct funnel CTA. It's about 161 words, under 170. The title promise "Is it permanent?" is answered in the first sentence. There are five minor fixes. Two are source tags that don't support their lines (s5 and s7). One is a small hedge in s1. One is the NHS year, and one notes that AAFP gives a different timeline.

issues.claim: See a doctor if shedding lasts more than about six months, comes out in patches, or your scalp looks scarred
issues.problem: None of the cited sources sets the 6-month cutoff. DermNet only says chronic shedding can last 'long periods… sometimes for years'. The NHS page I fetched supports only 'if you're worried'. The cutoff is supported by Asghar et al., Cureus 2020, which defines chronic telogen effluvium as lasting more than six months and calls the condition diffuse and non-scarring. DermNet backs the patchy differential (diffuse alopecia areata).
issues.fix: Add source src6: Asghar F et al. 'Telogen Effluvium: A Review of the Literature.' Cureus 2020;12(5):e8320, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7320655/. Set s5 source_ids to ["src6", "src3", "src2"]. Keep the narration as it is.

issues.claim: Don't stop or change your medicines on your own. Not personal advice…
issues.problem: These are the channel's own safety lines, but they're tagged to the Zepbound label (src4), which doesn't say them.

issues.claim: More hair in your brush on tirzepatide? Good news: it usually isn't permanent.
issues.problem: 'Usually isn't permanent' comes from telogen effluvium data in general, not from tirzepatide trials. s2 makes this clear, but s1 could add a light hedge.
